Compare a zinbreg fit with an nbreg fit

Source: R/inference.R
vuong_test.Rd

Compares the zero-inflated model with the plain negative binomial (NB) model fitted to the same data. It reports the Vuong statistics as a descriptive comparison and, with B > 0, a parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio (LR) test of NB against the zero-inflated model.

Usage

vuong_test(m1, m2, B = 0, alpha = 0.05, seed = NULL, progress = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'nbzinbreg_vuong'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

Arguments

m1, m2

A zinbreg fit and an nbreg fit to the same data, in either order.

B

Number of bootstrap replicates for the LR test; 0 (the default) skips it.

alpha

Significance level for the bootstrap decision.

seed

NULL, or a whole number for set.seed() (bootstrap only).

progress

Logical; if TRUE, report bootstrap progress.

...

Not used (an error if supplied), except for print().

x

An nbzinbreg_vuong object, for print().

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

Value

An object of class nbzinbreg_vuong, a list with:

  • statistic and p.value: the raw, AIC- and BIC-corrected statistics, and their p-values;

  • favours: the model each statistic favours;

  • N, k, models, mean and sd of the log ratios, and notes;

  • bootstrap: NULL without the bootstrap. Otherwise the LR statistic, p.value, p.bounds, used, failures, conclusive, reasons, reject, the replicate statuses and statistics, and the seed.

Details

Vuong statistics. With m_i = log p1(y_i) - log p2(y_i) (models in the order given), N the number of observations, and k1, k2 the numbers of coefficients (theta not counted, as in pscl::vuong()), the raw statistic is sqrt(N) mean(m) / sd(m). The AIC- and BIC-corrected versions subtract (k1 - k2) / N and (k1 - k2) log(N) / (2 N) from the mean. A positive statistic favours model 1, a negative one model 2. The p-values are one-sided in that direction, as in pscl::vuong(). Frequency weights count as repeated observations: N = sum(w) and the weighted mean and variance (divisor N - 1) are those of the expanded data. Weights must therefore be whole numbers.

The Vuong test is not a valid test of zero inflation. The NB model is the boundary pi = 0 of the zero-inflated model, so the models are nested at a boundary point rather than non-nested. Under the NB model the statistic does not have its normal reference distribution. The statistics are reported as a descriptive comparison only; use the bootstrap LR test for inference.

Bootstrap LR test (B > 0). The null hypothesis is the NB model. Its requirements:

  • the NB model is the count part of the zero-inflated one (the same covariate space and offset);

  • the zero part has an intercept, so pi -> 0 gives the NB model;

  • both fits have converged;

  • the weights are whole numbers.

The observed statistic is LR = 2 (l_ZINB - l_NB). Here l_ZINB is the supremum over the closure of the zero-inflated model: the largest of the supplied fit, a refit started at the NB boundary (pi near 0), and l_NB itself. So LR >= 0, and differences within 1e-6 (|l_NB| + 1) count as 0.

B data sets are simulated from the NB fit (a row of weight w gives w independent draws). Each is refitted under both models. The NB refit starts from the estimates, then from the default start. The zero-inflated refits start from the default start and from the NB boundary, and the higher log-likelihood is used.

Data sets whose estimate lies on a boundary are valid samples:

  • with no zeros, only zeros, or a collapsed zero part, LR = 0;

  • near pi = 0, the score at pi = 0 decides. If it is positive (the likelihood rises into the interior), a collapsed result is refitted from an interior start, and fails if it collapses again;

  • if every zero-inflated refit stops unconverged, the data set is accepted at pi -> 0 only on the evidence described in boot_se().

Anything else is a numerical failure. Examples are a refit that cannot be completed, NB theta on a bound that is not the Poisson limit, and a zero-inflated refit ending below the NB refit (also an nbzinbreg_warning_monotone warning).

p-value with failures. With B_u usable replicates, F failures and c usable replicates with LR* >= LR, there are three p-values:

  • p = (1 + c) / (B_u + 1) (failures dropped);

  • p_lo = (1 + c) / (B + 1) (every failure counted as below LR);

  • p_hi = (1 + c + F) / (B + 1) (every failure counted as at or above).

Failures may be selected (unusual data sets fail more often), so the bounds decide. The test is inconclusive when p_lo <= alpha < p_hi, when more than 10% of the replicates failed, or when fewer than 99 are usable.

The bootstrap is approximate. It simulates from the estimated NB model, and inherits any misfit of that model; the parameters other than the zero part are interior, so it is consistent. Each replicate needs two EM fits, so B = 199 takes a while; progress = TRUE reports progress.

Errors and warnings

  • nbzinbreg_error_input:

    • not one zinbreg and one nbreg fit;

    • fits to different data (rows, response or weights);

    • non-integer frequency weights;

    • an invalid B, alpha, seed or progress, or unused arguments;

    • for B > 0: an NB model that is not the count part, no zero-part intercept, or a data set of more than 1e7 draws.

  • nbzinbreg_error_fit: B > 0 with a fit that did not converge.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_convergence: a fit did not converge (the Vuong p-values are then NA), or the supplied zinbreg fit is below a refit from the NB boundary.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_bootstrap: failed replicates, or an inconclusive test.

  • nbzinbreg_warning_monotone: replicates whose zero-inflated refit ended below the NB refit.

See also

overdispersion_test(), anova.zinbreg(), boot_se()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(200))
d$y <- ifelse(runif(200) < 0.3, 0, rnbinom(200, size = 2, mu = exp(1 + d$x)))
z <- zinbreg(y ~ x | 1, data = d)
n <- nbreg(y ~ x, data = d)
vuong_test(z, n)
#> 
#> Vuong comparison: model 1 (zinbreg) vs model 2 (nbreg), N = 200
#> 
#>               z statistic Favours p-value
#> Raw                 1.915 model 1 0.02777
#> AIC-corrected       1.618 model 1 0.05281
#> BIC-corrected       1.129 model 1 0.12937
#> 
#> Note: the NB model is the boundary pi = 0 of the zero-inflated model, so the
#> Vuong test is not a valid test of zero inflation; the statistics are descriptive.
# \donttest{
# a short run (too few replicates for a conclusion: use B = 199 or more)
vuong_test(z, n, B = 19, seed = 1)
#> Warning: vuong_test(): 1 of 19 bootstrap replicates failed; the p-value is reported with bounds that count every failure as below or as at or above the observed statistic. The bootstrap test is inconclusive: the failed replicates could change the decision at alpha = 0.05 (p between 0.05 and 0.1); only 18 usable replicates (at least 99 are needed). First failure: the zero-inflated refits did not converge, and the sample is not at the pi -> 0 boundary: the score at pi = 0 is positive (D = 0.292), so the likelihood rises into the interior.
#> 
#> Vuong comparison: model 1 (zinbreg) vs model 2 (nbreg), N = 200
#> 
#>               z statistic Favours p-value
#> Raw                 1.915 model 1 0.02777
#> AIC-corrected       1.618 model 1 0.05281
#> BIC-corrected       1.129 model 1 0.12937
#> 
#> Note: the NB model is the boundary pi = 0 of the zero-inflated model, so the
#> Vuong test is not a valid test of zero inflation; the statistics are descriptive.
#> 
#> Parametric bootstrap likelihood-ratio test of NB against ZINB
#>   LR = 12.92 (log-likelihoods: NB -407.2, ZINB -400.8)
#>   Replicates: 19 (18 usable: 13 interior, 5 on a boundary; 1 failed)
#>   p-value = 0.05263  [0.05, 0.1] counting failures as below / at or above LR
#>   Inconclusive: the failed replicates could change the decision at alpha = 0.05 (p between 0.05 and 0.1); only 18 usable replicates (at least 99 are needed)
# }
